lessons.title: Media experiences
objectives: Relate media experiences and distinguish finished from current relevance.
Develop a connected response in a discussion about media experiences with a reason and relevant detail.

content_sections.title: Notice the connected language (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read this model: 'I have considered media experiences, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.' Identify the main point, the linking expression, and the supporting detail. Then explain how the wording helps the speaker achieve this objective: Relate media experiences and distinguish finished from current relevance.

content_sections.title: Guided exchange (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work with a partner in a discussion about media experiences. Give a clear main point, support it with a specific reason, and respond to one follow-up question. Use tactful language when the other speaker presents a different perspective.

content_sections.title: Independent connected response (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Prepare a one-minute response about media experiences. Organize it into thought groups, stress the words that carry your main point, and finish with a concise conclusion rather than a list of isolated sentences.

exercises.prompt: Choose the most connected and tactful response for a discussion about media experiences.
options: I have considered media experiences, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
Media experiences is a topic, but I will not explain my view.
Several details exist about media experiences, perhaps.
exercises.correct_answer: I have considered media experiences, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.

exercises.prompt: Complete this response about media experiences: 'My experience supports this view ____.'
acceptable_answers: because it offers evidence about media experiences

exercises.prompt: Read the short response about media experiences and identify how the writer handles another view.
exercises.stimulus: Although another person may disagree about media experiences, I can respond politely and explain my reason.

questions.question: How does the writer respond to disagreement?
acceptable_answers: The writer responds politely and gives a reason in the discussion of media experiences.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 60–90 seconds in a discussion about media experiences. State your point, support it, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Presents a connected main point about media experiences with relevant support.
Responds clearly and tactfully to a follow-up question about media experiences.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short response about media experiences. Identify the view and supporting reason before the transcript is revealed, then listen again to check the linking language.
listening.goal: Follow the main point and support in spoken language about media experiences.
listening.transcript: I have considered media experiences, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
listening.question: What view and supporting reason does the speaker communicate?
listening.answer: The speaker connects a considered view about media experiences to a useful reason from experience.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay a discussion about media experiences. Learner role: present and support a view. Tutor role: ask one probing question and offer a different perspective. End after the learner responds tactfully and summarizes the point.
speaking.goal: Sustain a connected, tactful exchange about media experiences.
constraints: State both roles before beginning the exchange.
Use at most four tutor turns and stop after the learner summary.

pronunciation.instruction: Record the model about media experiences in meaningful thought groups. Stress the main point and reason, then compare a second attempt with the first for clarity and rhythm.
pronunciation.goal: Make connected speech about media experiences easy to follow.
pronunciation.target: Thought groups and information stress for media experiences
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write 90–120 words about media experiences. State a position or experience, support it with a reason and example, and acknowledge another perspective. Submit your own draft before asking for feedback.
writing.goal: Produce a connected written response about media experiences.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
